Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The Indian players are out in the middle. Renuka Singh to bowl first. Beth Mooney and Alyssa Healy to open for the Aussies. Let's play...
...THE CHASE...

Australia Women will be happy with how they bowled. They had to win this match to stay alive and bowled with great determination. Alyssa Healy would have taken this score at the start. Kim Garth, Annabel Sutherland and Georgia Wareham ended with two each. All in all, it was a solid performance from Australia Women. If the dew comes in, this could be a pretty straightforward win for the Aussies however, India will try their best to make each run count. Stay tuned.

The last two overs have given India runs. Still not enough but they have extra runs to fight with. India though were wavy at the start. The top four who make the bulk of the runs were pretty disappointing and fell near the halfway mark. However, Richa Ghosh and Deepti Sharma showed intent while batting and put on a fight but that too didn't last long. Ghosh fell but Deepti Sharma stayed till the end and made sure India Women end with a fighting total.

OUT! RUN OUT! A run out to end the innings! Megan Schutt on a fuller length, on middle and leg, Deepti Sharma swings hard but only manages to get an inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls away towards square leg and Alyssa Healy gives it a chase. The batters complete the single and with it being the last ball, they decide to come back for the second run. Ellyse Perry swoops in from the deep and releases an accurate throw towards Beth Mooney who has made her way towards the stumps at the batting end. Mooney collects it cleanly and does the rest to catch Deepti well short of her crease. India Women finish with 130!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the second T20I to begin as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. Alyssa Healy leads her troops out to the centre now and they are joined by the two Indian openers. It will be Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana to open the innings for India Women. Megan Schutt will start with the new ball for Australia Women. Off we go...

PITCH REPORT - Melanie Jones is near the deck. She starts by saying that pitch number 6 will be used for this game. Shares that the square boundaries are 64 and 58 metres long while it is a 70-metre hit down the ground. Feels that dew is an important factor at this venue. Further adds that the ground staff have put an anti-dew spray on the outfield to reduce the dew effect. Reckons that ball will be easier to grip and it might not skid on as it did in the first T20I. States that there is less live grass on this surface but there is an even covering of grass. Feels that the seamers will do well while bowling first. Adds that spinners might not get a lot of turn but they will still have a role to play.

The captain of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says that they would have looked to bowl first as well. Feels that that this pitch is better than the previous game and it is less sticky as compared to the previous surface. Reckons that batting first is also a good option. States that Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana gave them a fair idea about the boundary options through their batting in the first game. Ends by informing that they are going with the same team as the last game.

Alyssa Healy, the skipper of Australia Women, says that they will bowl first. Adds that dew is a big factor but they want to start well and take some early wickets. Reckons they know what lies ahead with the World Cup coming up but they want to do well in the matches leading to that. Informs they have made one change with Kim Garth coming in for Darcie Brown.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (C/WK), Beth Mooney, Tahlia McGrath, Ellyse Perry, Ashleigh Gardner, Phoebe Litchfield, Grace Harris, Annabel Sutherland, Georgia Wareham, Kim Garth (In for Darcie Brown), Megan Schutt.

India Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Deepti Sharma, Amanjot Kaur, Richa Ghosh (WK), Pooja Vastrakar, Shreyanka Patil, Titas Sadhu, Renuka Singh.
TOSS - Alyssa Healy calls it correctly and Australia Women have opted to BOWL first.

The Indian bowlers were a dominating force in the first match. They did a commendable job by restricting Australia Women to a below-par score and later, chasing it quite convincingly. To keep the series alive, Australia Women have to put in a much better performance. They might want to brush of the first game and bounce back to make it 1-1. Can they do it though or India Women will clinch the series? We will find out soon. Toss coming up.

Hello and welcome to the second T20I of the 3-match series between Australia Women and India Women. Australia Women started the white-ball series well by winning 3-0 but were put under pressure by the 19-year old sensation Titas Sadhu who ran through the Aussie line up and picked four wickets. It was quite an easy win for India Women but expect Australia Women to bounce back strongly in this second match.
...MATCH DAY...

After a dominating performance in the first T20I, India Women would be itching to take on Australia Women in the 2nd T20I of the 3-match T20I series at the Dr. DY Patil Sports Academy, Navi Mumbai. The Women in Blue lead the 3-match T20I series 1-0. The hosts after winning the One-off Test the hosts were later dismentaled by the Aussies in the 3-match ODI series losing all 3 but bouncing back and in some style with a demolishing of the visitors by 9 wickets in the 1st T20I. It was the 19-year-old Indian Pacer Titas Sadhu who ran riots at the Aussie batting unit and pinned them back to the wall. She was very well supported by others too in restricting the Australia Women to a below-par total which was chased down clinically and convincingly by India Women. Openers Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma found good form as they both struck their respective half-centuries. The Women in Blue would be looking to replicate a similar sort of performance and clinch the T20I series in the 2nd game itself. The visitors on the other hand had a horrible time with the bat but were bailed to an extent by their young sensation Phoebe Litchfield. The batting unit failed as only Ellyse Perry and Phoebe Litchfield put up a fight of any sort but the other couldn't get going. The bowlers did not perform as expected of them as well and they failed to shake up the Indian batting line-up leading them to a heavy defeat. The visitors would be looking to bounce back and they have got all the armory in the arsenal to bounce back against a highly confident India Women's side. Expect a cracker when these two sides collide.
